This course follows a simulated genotyping study from laboratory exports to
association results. You do not need previous programming experience. Read one
step, run its R command in the RStudio console, and compare the result before
continuing. Keep your computer's language and decimal settings as they are.

Validation: executable preparation chunks passed on Windows. Installer actions and the masked RStudio prompt remain manual checks.

This notebook is the source for the guided preparation module. The older
`01_quality_control.Rmd` belongs to a separate, smaller demonstration.

```{r module0_knit_root, include=FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else ".."))
}
```

## 0.1 What you need {#step-0-1}

### What we do

Prepare a computer, a project folder and the tools used throughout the course.

### Why

R is the language that runs our commands. RStudio provides a console, file
browser and editor around R. PLINK 2 is a separate program that processes
genotypes. A genotype records the alleles observed at a DNA site. R starts
PLINK for you, but installing R does not install PLINK.

### You need

A Windows, macOS or Linux computer; an internet connection for software and
the approved data download; and a writable folder. The local data test does
not require a network download. Keep space for the encrypted archive, an
extracted copy and intermediate results. Required space grows as you work.

### Command

Once R is installed, this safe command identifies your operating system:

```{r s0-1_system}
Sys.info()[c("sysname", "release", "machine")]
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript -e "print(Sys.info())"`. `-e` evaluates the R
expression in quotes. Do not paste terminal commands into the R console.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

A named list of system information: Windows, Darwin (macOS), or Linux, with
your own system release and processor. These values depend on your computer.
They are not genotype counts.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

If `Sys.info()` is not recognised, check that you are typing in the R console,
which normally displays `>`. Continue with step 0.2 if R is not installed yet.

</details>

### Quick check

Does installing R also install the program that analyses the genotype files?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. PLINK 2 is installed separately at step 0.4.</details>

### Files created

None.

## 0.2 Install R {#step-0-2}

### What we do

Install R from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/). Select your operating
system and its installation package. On Linux, follow CRAN's instructions for
your distribution; package installation may require an administrator.

### Why

The R interpreter reads the commands in the notebooks. A package adds
functions to R; packages do not replace R itself.

### You need

The system and processor identified at 0.1. On Apple Silicon use the ARM64
build; Intel Macs use the Intel build. Do not mix processor builds.

### Command

Open R after installation and run:

```{r s0-2_r_version}
R.version.string
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript --version`. `--version` prints the installed
version without running an analysis. If the terminal cannot find Rscript but
RStudio can run R, use the R console; terminal PATH setup is not required here.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

A line beginning `R version`. The version on your computer may differ from
the Windows validation environment, R 4.5.2. Ubuntu extraction was also tested
by the author using R 4.6.1.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

If installation is blocked, ask the instructor or your institution's support
team for an approved installation. Do not change your system language.

</details>

### Quick check

What does the version command measure: the version of R or the version of PLINK?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>The version of R.</details>

### Files created

The R installer creates software files outside this course project.

## 0.3 Install RStudio {#step-0-3}

### What we do

Install [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) and open it.
Choose the build for your operating system. R must already be installed.

### Why

The console runs commands now. The editor keeps commands in a notebook so you
can read and rerun them later. R objects in memory disappear when R restarts;
saved output files remain on disk.

### You need

A working R installation from 0.2 and the RStudio installer.

### Command

In the RStudio console, run this small calculation:

```{r s0-3_console}
2 + 3
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript -e "print(2 + 3)"`. The console and terminal
use the same R calculation. RStudio itself is opened through your applications menu.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

`[1] 5`. The `[1]` labels the first value printed; it is not part of the answer.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

If RStudio cannot find R, check that R was installed for the correct processor.
Restart RStudio after installing R. A `+` prompt usually means an unfinished
command; press Escape and enter the complete command again.

</details>

### Quick check

After restarting R, should you expect an unsaved object to remain in memory?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Reload it from a saved file or rerun the command that creates it.</details>

### Files created

RStudio software files. No course data are created by the calculation.

## 0.4 Download PLINK 2 {#step-0-4}

### What we do

Get the latest matching build from the [official PLINK 2 page](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/).
Extract the executable into the project's `bin/` folder. The executable is
`plink2.exe` on Windows and `plink2` on macOS or Linux. Extract it first;
the ZIP file is not the executable.

### Why

PLINK 2 reads the genotype formats and computes QC and association statistics.
PLINK 1.9 is a different program. Tested version information is held once in
`config.R`; the setup check reports your version and warns if it differs.

### You need

Your system and processor from 0.1 and the extracted project from 0.5.
You may download the executable first and copy it after extracting the project.

### Command

After opening the project at 0.6, read the configured tested version:

```{r s0-4_plink_setting}
settings <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
sys.source("config.R", settings)
settings$course_settings$tested_plink_version
```

Terminal equivalent for checking the executable: `bin/plink2 --version`
(Windows: `bin\plink2.exe --version`). `--version` requests the version string;
it does not read data. The R setup check performs this call for you at 0.7.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The configured tested PLINK 2 version is printed. At 0.7 the installed binary
must identify itself as PLINK v2. A newer version produces a warning rather
than an automatic failure solely because its version differs.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

On macOS or Linux an extracted executable may need execute permission. In a
terminal at the project root, `chmod u+x bin/plink2` grants your user execute
permission for that file. If institutional security blocks it, ask support.
Do not disable computer security controls.

</details>

### Quick check

Can a file named `plink2.zip` be used as the executable?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Extract the matching executable from it.</details>

### Files created

`bin/plink2.exe` or `bin/plink2`, outside version control.

## 0.5 Download the course package {#step-0-5}

### What we do

Download and extract the whole source project from its GitHub branch. Then
obtain the matching encrypted data archive through the approved course channel.
The GitHub Release does not exist yet: the current archive is a local author
test. Its checksums are marked as test values in `config.R`.

### Why

The source project contains code and text. The encrypted package contains
data. Checksums detect changed downloads; the password decrypts the archive.
A correct password does not replace checksum verification.

### You need

The complete project folder, R and the approved archive. For the author test,
set `COURSE_WORK_DIR` to the existing external work folder before using the
local command below. The instructor supplies the password separately.

### Command

Run the following interactively after opening the project. It is not run
automatically when rendering this notebook:

```{r s0-5_data, eval=FALSE}
source("R/package_setup.R")
install_course_packages()
source("R/course.R")
# For the published release, after its approved URLs and checksums are configured:
download_course_data()
```

For the local test, use this instead; it makes no network download:

```{r s0-5_local, eval=FALSE}
download_course_data(
  zip_path = file.path(Sys.getenv("COURSE_WORK_DIR"), "release", "course-data-2026.1.zip")
)
```

`download_course_data` uses `getPass` to ask for a masked password. Do not
write the password in this notebook, a shared script or your command history.
There is no separate terminal decryption command for students. Both routes
use the same R helper and `archive`; no 7-Zip installation is required.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

For the local stage 1 archive: `Course data are ready: 55 files verified.`
The destination is `data/course/`. The archive and sidecar manifest must both
match their configured SHA-256 values; all extracted payload files are checked.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

An empty release URL means the public release has not been configured. Use
the authorised local test or ask the instructor. A wrong password produces a
message asking you to check typing and contact the instructor if needed.
Never bypass a checksum failure. An existing destination is refused to protect
your work. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

If the checksum differs but the password is accepted, should you use that download?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. Obtain the approved matching package before continuing.</details>

### Files created

Verified data under `data/course/`. Temporary download and extraction files
are removed. Data and passwords are never added to Git.

## 0.6 Open the project {#step-0-6}

### What we do

Open `GWAS_training_session.Rproj` from the extracted folder. In RStudio,
open this notebook from `lessons/`. Run commands in the console at the project root.

### Why

Relative paths are interpreted from the working directory. Keeping one project
root avoids copying your personal absolute paths into every command.

### You need

The complete extracted project from 0.5, not an individual downloaded notebook.

### Command

```{r s0-6_project}
getwd()
stopifnot(file.exists("config.R"), file.exists("R/course.R"))
```

Terminal equivalent: from the project directory, run
`Rscript -e "stopifnot(file.exists('config.R'))"`. `stopifnot` stops when a
required condition is false. No output means this check passed.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Your project folder is printed. The file checks finish without an error.
Your personal folder path will differ from the author's path.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

If `config.R` is absent, reopen the project from the extracted source folder.
Do not create a blank replacement or rename a downloaded HTML page to `.R`.

</details>

### Quick check

Does a relative path starting `R/` refer to a folder on every computer's C drive?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. It refers to the R folder under the current project root.</details>

### Files created

RStudio may create local project settings under `.Rproj.user/`; they are ignored by Git.

## 0.7 Run the setup check {#step-0-7}

### What we do

Check packages, locale, genotype file integrity and a small PLINK read/write operation.

### Why

A program can print its version while still failing to read data or write
results in a path containing spaces and non-English characters. Testing a
real operation catches these failures before a long analysis.

### You need

The executable from 0.4 and verified data from 0.5. The standard guided folder
is `data/course/`. For an existing external installation, `COURSE_DATA_DIR`
may identify the extracted data and `COURSE_OUTPUT_DIR` a separate output folder.
These optional environment variables contain paths, never passwords.

### Command

```{r s0-7_preflight}
source("scripts/preflight.R")
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript --vanilla scripts/preflight.R`. `--vanilla`
starts without saved workspaces and startup files. Internally the R helper
runs PLINK with `--bfile` (input BED/BIM/FAM prefix), `--autosome` (autosomal
sites), `--thin-count 20` (a small subset), `--seed 20261111` (repeatable sampling),
`--freq` (allele frequencies) and `--out` (output prefix). The exact command,
including your paths and resource settings, is printed and recorded.

For the standard project layout, the plain PLINK command is:

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/lab_export/sim2026_lab --autosome --thin-count 20 --seed 20261111 --freq --out results/guided/s0-7_probe --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--threads 2` limits worker threads; `--memory 2048` sets the main workspace
budget in MiB. On Windows the executable is `bin\plink2.exe`. The helper's
regression probe intentionally uses a non-English path and translates it safely.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The guided starting data have 2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variants. Wells
include replicates; there are 2,000 simulated people. PLINK completes the
20-variant frequency probe and R prints `Preflight passed. Report:` followed
by the report path. The package installation check may print additional messages.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. The setup check explains unavailable packages or a
missing PLINK binary. On Windows it clears inherited locale requests that R
cannot use, for this session only; startup warnings can appear before the
script has a chance to run. Your Windows language stays unchanged. On Linux,
the package preparation selects matching Posit binaries where available and
explains development libraries if source installation is needed. Do not run
later analytical steps until the setup check succeeds.

</details>

### Quick check

Why does the setup check write a frequency report rather than only print a version?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>It tests actual data reading and file writing, including a path containing spaces and non-English characters.</details>

### Files created

`results/guided/software_versions.txt`, `results/guided/preflight.txt` and
PLINK probe reports under its `path check/` folder. If `COURSE_OUTPUT_DIR` is
set, the same files are written there instead. No source input is changed.

## 0.8 How to use this guide {#step-0-8}

### What we do

Use the same reading, running and checking routine at every step.

### Why

Running all commands at once makes the first mistake harder to locate.
Saving files gives you a route back after a restart without relying on an R workspace.

### You need

A successful check at 0.7. Keep the output files and the notebook together in
their documented locations. The [glossary](../docs/glossary.md) explains terms
used in the course, including quality control, alleles and association.

### Command

Read your supplied checkpoint inventory without changing any files:

```{r s0-8_progress}
where_am_i(data_dir = cfg$data_dir, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

Terminal equivalent: invoke the R helper through Rscript after setting the
same project paths. There is no PLINK command for reporting course progress.
`check_step("3.2")` compares that step with a supplied checkpoint;
`restore_checkpoint("3.2")` restores step 3.1 so that you can restart 3.2.
Both protect existing output folders.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Before analysis, states in the updated checkpoint index are `not verified`.
Full genotype boundaries are 2.8, 3.8, 4.6 and 5.7; intermediate states are
reconstructed from stored lists and transformations. Diagnostic and analysis
files have separate small checkpoints. The unchanged original 55-file stage 1
test ZIP uses the older layout: full filesets only at 4.6 and 5.6, with other
folders reported as `reference lists only`. Use the updated staged package for
the new main-path restart routes; do not mix the two layouts.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

A missing checkpoint is not evidence that you failed the analysis. It can mean
the course package does not supply the required baseline, lists or index. Ask
for the matching updated package; do not mix versions or claim that copying
a list alone recreated genotypes.

</details>

### Quick check

To restart step 4.2, which completed step's files do you need?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>Step 4.1, from the same course data version.</details>

### Files created

None by `where_am_i`. Continue to module 1, which explains how the array data arise.
